titulo: The five questions everyone asks you
subtitulo: Where you're from, how long you're staying, whether you like it here — ready answers so the conversation keeps moving instead of stalling on you
cena: The same five questions are coming, in roughly the same order, from a taxi driver, a shopkeeper and a stranger at a bar — and having the answers ready is the difference between a conversation and a stall.
decisao: ter respostas prontas pras mesmas 4-5 perguntas que todo mundo faz, em vez de improvisar toda vez — isso mantém a conversa andando
frasePiso: The questions repeat almost word for word. Your answers can too.

steps.pt: Almost every stranger asks some version of the same four or five questions — good news, you can walk in with real answers ready.

steps.promptPt: Answer with where you're actually from. Speak now.

steps.pt: This one wants a real number, not a philosophy. Keep it short.

steps.promptPt: Give your real length of stay. Speak now.

steps.es: ¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?
steps.pt: What have you liked most about Mexico?
steps.tts: ¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?

steps.pt: This question makes it warm, not transactional — a specific answer beats a generic 'everything.'

steps.promptPt: Give one specific thing you've genuinely liked. Speak now.
steps.es: Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.
steps.pinyin: meh en-kahn-TOH lah koh-MEE-dah, SOH-breh TOH-doh lohs TAH-kohs
steps.pt: I loved the food, especially the tacos.
steps.tts: Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.

steps.pt: Are you traveling alone or with family?

steps.promptPt: Say who you're travelling with, or that you're on your own. Speak now.

steps.pt: And if you want out of a conversation, that's fine too — one polite line closes it without rudeness.

steps.promptPt: You need to get going. Excuse yourself politely. Speak now.
steps.es: Bueno, fue un gusto. Que le vaya bien.
steps.pinyin: BWEH-noh, fweh oon GOOS-toh. keh leh BAH-yah byen
steps.pt: Well, it was nice talking to you. Take care.
steps.tts: Bueno, fue un gusto. Que le vaya bien.

steps.promptPt: Turn the small talk into a plan. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there anything to see nearby?

steps.promptPt: They clearly know the city. Ask them. Speak now.
Open the door before walking through it. Speak now.
They have been generous. Ask for one more thing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have any advice for me?

steps.es: Soy de Estados Unidos. Diez días, más o menos. Me encantó la comida.
steps.pinyin: soy deh ehs-TAH-dohs oo-NEE-dohs. DYEHS DEE-ahs, mahs oh MEH-nohs. meh en-kahn-TOH lah koh-MEE-dah
steps.pt: Shadow the three most common answers in a row.
steps.tts: Soy de Estados Unidos. Diez días, más o menos. Me encantó la comida.

steps.pt: I05 complete. Origin, duration, what you've liked, who you're with — have real answers ready, and know how to leave well too.

secoes.corpo: 'Me encantó todo' is a safe answer but a flat one. Naming one real thing — a dish, a place, a person — gives the other person something to respond to, and the conversation actually continues.

secoes.titulo: A short number is a complete answer
secoes.corpo: Diez días, más o menos is enough. Nobody needs your itinerary; the question is usually just a warm-up, not a request for detail.

secoes.titulo: Leaving well is a skill, not an afterthought
secoes.corpo: Que le vaya bien or fue un gusto closes a conversation with a stranger warmly, without the exchange having to trail off awkwardly.

permissao: You are allowed to reuse the exact same three sentences all week. Nobody is grading you on originality — the questions repeat because they're genuinely just how people open a friendly conversation, not a test you need fresh answers for each time.
espelho: Small talk with a stranger anywhere in the world runs on the same handful of questions — where are you from, how long are you here, what do you think of the place — and having a few ready answers is not a foreign skill, it's the same social shortcut everyone already uses at home.

fichasCulturais.sinal: A stranger — a taxi driver, a shopkeeper, someone at a bar — starts asking you personal-sounding questions almost immediately: where you're from, how long you're staying, whether you're travelling alone.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This feels intrusive, or they want something from me.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: This is standard, warm small talk in a lot of everyday Mexican interactions, not an unusual level of personal interest — it's the equivalent of 'so, where are you headed?' in many English-speaking small talk contexts, just a bit more direct.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer briefly and genuinely — origin, rough duration, one thing you've liked — and the conversation will move on naturally from there.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get a warmer, more human interaction instead of a purely transactional one, and often useful local tips along the way.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a signal to share sensitive details like your exact hotel, daily schedule, or valuables — normal friendliness doesn't require that level of specificity either.
